ancient_civilizations.name: Minoan Civilization
ancient_civilizations.description: Europe's first advanced civilization based on Crete; built multi-story palaces with advanced plumbing; used undeciphered Linear A script; dominated Mediterranean trade

ancient_civilizations.name: Neburu (Planet X / Nibiru)
ancient_civilizations.description: Larger planet home to the Amunaki race; collided with Earth creating the Grand Canyon and the Moon; survivors became pharaohs and kings before building spaceships and leaving

ancient_civilizations.name: Murder at the Gates of Uruk
ancient_civilizations.description: Epic of Gilgamesh murder mystery party game featuring 9 elite suspects where King Gilgamesh is poisoned by the Black Lotus toxin

historical_migrations.name: The Gothic War
historical_migrations.description: Thervingi Goths crossed into Roman Thrace fleeing Huns, weaponizing internal placement after abuse; destroyed eastern Roman army at Adrianople and killed the Emperor

historical_migrations.name: Anglo-Saxon Conquest
historical_migrations.description: Germanic settlers migrated across North Sea as family units, pushing Celtic Britons into Wales and Cornwall to create "England"

historical_migrations.name: Yayoi-Jōmon Displacement
historical_migrations.description: Wet-rice farmers migrated from Korean Peninsula into Japan with bronze weapons, outbreeding and replacing native Jōmon hunter-gatherers

historical_migrations.name: Amorite Infiltration
historical_migrations.description: Nomadic Semitic groups entered Sumer and Akkad due to global drought, overthrew the Sumerian state, and founded the first Babylonian Empire

historical_migrations.name: Yuezhi Conquest
historical_migrations.description: Nomadic pastoralists forced west by Xiongnu into Greco-Bactrian Kingdom, later building the Kushan Empire

historical_migrations.name: Vandal Conquest of North Africa
historical_migrations.description: 80,000 Vandals and Alans crossed the Straits of Gibraltar, captured Carthage, and established a maritime kingdom

historical_migrations.name: Doric Invasions of Greece
historical_migrations.description: Greek-speaking northern tribes migrated en masse into the Peloponnese, laying the cultural foundation for ancient Sparta

historical_migrations.name: Thule Displacement
historical_migrations.description: Thule people migrated eastward from Alaska to Greenland, replacing the Paleo-Inuit Dorset culture

historical_migrations.name: Philistine Settlement
historical_migrations.description: Aegean migrants settled southern Canaan with iron-working technology, establishing a powerful pentapolis

historical_migrations.name: Magna Graecia Colonisation
historical_migrations.description: Greek citizens migrated to southern Italy and Sicily, converting the region into a cultural powerhouse

historical_migrations.name: Slavic Migration into Balkans
historical_migrations.description: Decentralized Slavic families migrated southward toward the Danube River, resulting in the permanent Slavicisation of Southeastern Europe

historical_migrations.name: Mixtec Infiltration
historical_migrations.description: Mixtec families migrated into the Valley of Oaxaca using armed settlement and royal marriage alliances to take over Zapotec urban centers

american_military_contributions.name: American Revolution
american_military_contributions.description: Relied on foreign military leaders and immigrant volunteers (e.g., Marquis de Lafayette, Friedrich von Steuben) to transform raw colonial militias into a disciplined force

american_military_contributions.name: American Civil War
american_military_contributions.description: Roughly one in four Union soldiers (543,000 men) was foreign-born, providing the North with an insurmountable numerical and industrial advantage

american_military_contributions.name: World War II
american_military_contributions.description: Hundreds of thousands of first- and second-generation immigrants served in Allied armed forces and supplied vital wartime labor
